# v0.1.0 Critical correction pass (2026-11-23)

These owner instructions supersede the earlier design that showed 731 tiles (species plus forms).

## Pokédex
- One tile per species, grouped by generation. 649 is the Gen I–V **reference** count; it is labelled as such and never as the in-game Pokédex total.
- The 82 researched form records are kept and used only inside the Summary. Searching a form name (for example "wash", "chill drive" or "black kyurem") returns its parent species tile.
- The separate data axes are unchanged: reference catalog, in-game membership, wild, raids, roaming, events, storyline and player registration. Virizion, Cobalion and Terrakion remain permanent raids.
- Registration is per species. Choosing a form never creates a registration.

## Summary popup
- Clicking a Pokémon opens a large dialog inside the Companion, over the Pokédex. The right-hand `dex-layout split` panel has been removed.
- The grid stays mounted behind the dialog. Closing it (close button, Escape or a click on the backdrop) leaves search, filters and scroll position exactly as they were. If a registration was changed, the grid redraws at the same scroll position.
- A Form selector switches the verified types, stats, abilities and sprites. A form change with no verified source is badged "Form change not verified".
- All tabs, notes and registration work inside the popup. The Pokédex popout window still shows the Summary at a size that fits it.

## Reuse of local dump data
- On start, the app recovers any interrupted swap (`dex.prev` / `assets.prev`). Synchronisation then runs in a background thread instead of blocking start-up.
- It re-synchronises when the item catalogue is missing, when the install was made by an older importer, or when the source fingerprint has changed.
- The new data is built in temporary folders and then swapped in with rollback. If any rename fails, the previous `dex` and `assets` are restored.
- During automatic sync, a source that would install less than the current data (fewer species, sprites, icons or battle data) is refused, and the installed data is kept.
- If the original dump folder no longer exists, the Pokémon data stays installed, and the Item Library says plainly that it needs a one-time reinstall from the folder with `ItemSpriteDump.zip` and `PokedexData.zip`.
- User data is never touched by sync: runs, notes, registration, favourites, settings, window geometry and backups.

## Verification
- Backend tests, with dumps and without.
- Real-dump sync tests: fresh install, legacy (dex-1) upgrade, failed swap, interrupted swap, partial source and moved source.
- Playwright UI suites.

Native KDE/Wayland and Windows shells have not been verified here.
